facts.statement: Sebecus is an extinct genus of terrestrial, carnivorous crocodylomorph that lived in South America during the Paleogene period.
facts.quote: Sebecus (meaning "Sobek" in Latin) is an extinct genus of sebecid crocodylomorph from Paleogene period of South America.

facts.statement: The genus Sebecus currently includes two valid species: the type species S. icaeorhinus and S. ayrampu.
facts.quote: The genus is currently represented by two species, the type S. icaeorhinus and S. ayrampu.

facts.statement: American paleontologist George Gaylord Simpson named the genus Sebecus in 1937, making it one of the earliest known sebecosuchians.
facts.quote: Named by American paleontologist George Gaylord Simpson in 1937, Sebecus was one of the first known sebecosuchians.

facts.statement: Simpson described the type species S. icaeorhinus based on a fragmented skull and lower jaw discovered in the Sarmiento Formation.
facts.quote: Simpson described the type species, S. icaeorhinus, from a fragmented skull and lower jaw found in the Sarmiento Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered by the American Museum of Natural History's First Scarritt Expedition to Patagonia between 1930 and 1931.
facts.quote: The specimen was discovered by the American Museum of Natural History's First Scarritt Expedition to Patagonia, during 1930 and 1931.

facts.statement: Teeth attributed to Sebecus were first identified by Argentine paleontologist Florentino Ameghino in 1906, initially associated with carnivorous dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Teeth had been known since 1906 when Argentine paleontologist Florentino Ameghino associated them with carnivorous dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Sebecus possessed unusual ziphodont dentition characterized by teeth that were laterally compressed and serrated.
facts.quote: He noted its unusual ziphodont dentition in which the teeth were laterally compressed and serrated.

facts.statement: In 1965, Wann Langston Jr. named the species S. huilensis from Miocene fossils found at the La Venta locality in Colombia.
facts.quote: In 1965, American paleontologist Wann Langston, Jr. named a second species, S. huilensis, from the Miocene Honda Group at the La Venta locality in Colombia.

facts.statement: Remains were described from the Miocene of Peru in 1977.
facts.quote: In 1977, remains were described from the Miocene of Peru.

facts.statement: The species S. querejazus was named in 1991 from early Paleocene fossils found in the Santa Lucia Formation in Bolivia.
facts.quote: A third species of Sebecus, S. querejazus, was named in 1991 from the early Paleocene Santa Lucia Formation in Bolivia.

facts.statement: A new species was described by Bravo et al. in 2021 based on remains found in north-western Argentina.
facts.quote: In 2021 another species was described by Bravo et al. based on remains that were found in north-western Argentina.

facts.statement: Sebecus has been placed in various positions within the group of metasuchian crocodyliforms.
facts.quote: Sebecus has been placed in various positions among metasuchian crocodyliforms.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses suggest Sebecosuchia is polyphyletic, with Sebecus forming a metasuchian clade distantly related to Notosuchia.
facts.quote: Several recent phylogenetic analyses have resulted in a polyphyletic Sebecosuchia, with some members such as Baurusuchus being more closely related to notosuchians and other such as Sebecus forming a clade of metasuchians more distantly related to Notosuchia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Sebecus range from the Paleocene to the Mid Eocene, with possible records extending to the Late Miocene or Early Pliocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Paleocene - Mid EocenePossible Late Miocene-Early Pliocene record

facts.statement: The postcranial skeleton of S. icaeorhinus remained largely unknown until Pol et al. (2012) described remains including a partially articulated specimen MPEF-PV 1776.
facts.quote: The postcranial skeleton of S. icaeorhinus was virtually unknown until Pol et al. (2012) described postcranial remains of several individuals of this species, including a partially articulated specimen MPEF-PV 1776 with anterior region of the dentary (allowing the identification of this individual as representing S. icaeorhinus) and most of the postcranial skeleton preserved.

facts.statement: A 2007 study reclassified S. huilensis and S. querejazus into separate genera, Zulmasuchus and Langstonia, respectively.
facts.quote: A 2007 study of sebecids reclassified several species. The two species S. huilensis and S. querejazus were given their own genera, Zulmasuchus and Langstonia, respectively.

facts.statement: Sebecus was an extinct sebecid crocodylomorph that lived during the Eocene in present-day Patagonia, South America.
facts.quote: Sebecus (forma latinizada de "Sobek") es un género extinto de crocodilomorfo sebécido del Eoceno de la actual Patagonia (Suramérica).

facts.statement: The specimen MPEF-PV 1776 is estimated to have been between 2.2 and 3.1 meters long and weighed between 52.2 and 113.5 kilograms.
facts.quote: Estimates of total body length and mass of MPEF-PV 1776 vary from 2.2 to 3.1 m, and from 52.2 to 113.5 kg, respectively.

facts.statement: Unlike modern crocodilians, Sebecus possessed a deep and narrow snout.
facts.quote: Unlike modern crocodilians, Sebecus has a deep, narrow snout.

facts.statement: The nostrils of Sebecus opened at the very tip of its snout.
facts.quote: The nares, or nostrils, open anteriorly at the tip of the snout.

facts.statement: Sebecus is characterized by laterally compressed, ziphodont teeth.
facts.quote: Laterally compressed, or ziphodont teeth, are characteristic of Sebecus and other sebecosuchians.

facts.statement: The teeth at the tips of Sebecus's jaws were rounder in cross-section than those further back.
facts.quote: At the tips of the upper and lower jaws, the teeth are rounder in cross-section.

facts.statement: In Sebecus, the fourth tooth in the lower jaw was raised to function as an effective canine.
facts.quote: The fourth dentary tooth is raised in the lower jaw to form an effective canine.

facts.statement: The upper and lower teeth of Sebecus formed an alternating pattern that allowed the jaws to close tightly.
facts.quote: The teeth of the upper and lower jaws form an alternate pattern to allow the jaw to close tightly.

facts.statement: The jaw joint structure and broad downturned bones at the skull base restricted Sebecus's jaw movement to up-and-down motion.
facts.quote: Along with the broad downturned "wings" formed by the pterygoid and ectopterygoid bones at the bottom of the skull, this articulation restricts the jaw to up-and-down movement.

facts.statement: The deep skull and jaws of Sebecus provided more space for the adductor muscles that close the jaws.
facts.quote: In Sebecus, the shape of the skull and jaws provides more room for adductor muscles, or muscles that close the jaws.

facts.statement: Sebecus likely had a very strong jaw closure but a much weaker ability to open its jaws.
facts.quote: Therefore, while the closure of the jaws would have been very strong, the ability to open the jaws would be much weaker.

facts.statement: The genus Sebecus was described by Simpson in 1937.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Simpson, 1937

facts.statement: Sebecus belongs to the family Sebecidae.
facts.quote: familia: Sebecidae

facts.statement: The name Sebecus is a Latinization of Sebek (also called Sobek), the crocodile god of ancient Egypt.
facts.quote: El nombre Sebecus es una latinización de Sebek (también llamado Sobek), el dios cocodrilo del antiguo Egipto.

facts.statement: The species name icaeorhinus derives from Greek words meaning 'chance' or 'not according to plan' and 'snout', referring to the animal's unusually deep snout.
facts.quote: El nombre de especie icaeorhinus de la especie tipo se deriva de las palabras griegas εικαίοs, «azar» o «no de acuerdo al plan», y ρύγχος, «nariz», en referencia a la inusualmente profunda nariz del animal.

facts.statement: The postcranial skeleton of Sebecus provides evidence that it was fully terrestrial.
facts.quote: The postcranial skeleton of Sebecus provides additional evidence of its terrestriality.

facts.statement: The relatively wide supratemporal fenestrae at the top of Sebecus's skull allowed for the passage of large muscles.
facts.quote: The supratemporal fenestrae at the top of the skull are relatively wide, allowing for the passage of large muscles.

facts.statement: The Eustachian tubes in Sebecus were very complex, featuring several interconnected branches similar to those of crocodilians.
facts.quote: The Eustachian tubes, passages that connect the middle ear with the pharynx, are very complex in crocodilians.

facts.statement: In Sebecus, the olfactory bulb was elongate and made up a significant portion of the brain.
facts.quote: The olfactory bulb is elongate and makes up a significant portion of the brain.

facts.statement: The cerebrum of Sebecus was narrow and long compared to crocodilians, tapering toward the olfactory bulb.
facts.quote: The cerebrum is narrow and long in comparison to crocodilians, and tapers toward the olfactory bulb.

facts.statement: A 2001 study by Hans C. E. Larsson compared the cerebrum-to-total-brain volume ratio of Sebecus with that of the dinosaur Carcharodontosaurus saharicus and other prehistoric reptiles.
facts.quote: Hans C. E. Larsson performed a 2001 study of the endocranial anatomy of the dinosaur Carcharodontosaurus saharicus, comparing the ratio of its cerebrum to its total brain volume to the ratios of other prehistoric reptiles.

facts.statement: The genus Sebecus was first described by American paleontologist George Gaylord Simpson in 1937.
facts.quote: Sebecus, uno de los primeros sebecosuquios conocidos, fue descrito por el paleontólogo estadounidense George Gaylord Simpson en 1937.

facts.statement: The type species S. icaeorhinus was described based on fossils of a fragmented skull and a lower jaw.
facts.quote: Simpson describió la especie tipo, S. icaeorhinus, a partir de los fósiles de un cráneo fragmentado y una mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: The type specimen was discovered by the first Scarritt Expedition of the American Museum of Natural History in Patagonia.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue descubierto por la primera Expedición Scarritt del Museo Americano de Historia Natural a la Patagonia.

facts.statement: The teeth were known since 1906 when Argentine paleontologist Florentino Ameghino associated them with carnivorous dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Los dientes habían sido conocidos desde 1906 cuando el paleontólogo Argentino Florentino Ameghino los asoció con dinosaurios carnívoros.

facts.statement: The most complete material found by Simpson established that the animal was a crocodilomorph with an unusual ziphodont dentition where teeth are laterally compressed and serrated.
facts.quote: El material más completo, hallado por Simpson, estableció firmemente que el nuevo animal era un crocodilomorfo, aunque con una inusual dentición zifodonta, en la cual los dientes están lateralmente comprimidos y aserrados.

facts.statement: American paleontologist Edwin Harris Colbert completed Simpson's work by describing the genus exhaustively and placing it in the new family Sebecidae.
facts.quote: Otro paleontólogo estadounidense, Edwin Harris Colbert, completó el trabajo de Simpson, describiendo el género exhaustivamente y colocándolo en una nueva familia, Sebecidae.

facts.statement: Colbert placed Sebecus and the Cretaceous Baurusuchus in the order Sebecosuchia because both possessed high, deep snouts and ziphodont teeth.
facts.quote: Colbert situó a Sebecus y al baurusúquido del Cretácico Baurusuchus (también de Suramérica) en el orden Sebecosuchia (erigido por Simpson para todos los crocodilianos zifodontos), debido a que ambos poseían hocicos altos y profundos y dientes zifodontos.

facts.statement: In 1965, American paleontologist Wann Langston, Jr. described a second species, S. huilensis, from the La Venta paleontological site in Colombia.
facts.quote: En 1965, el paleontólogo estadounidense Wann Langston, Jr. describió una segunda especie, S. huilensis, del yacimiento paleontológico de La Venta (Mioceno) en Colombia.

facts.statement: The deposits date to the Laventense (about 12 million years old), extending the genus's temporal range in the Neogene by nearly 40 million years.
facts.quote: Los depósitos son del Laventense (una edad de la escala cronológica continental sudamericana basada en mamíferos, datada en unos 12 millones de años), extendiendo, por tanto, el rango temporal del género en el Neógeno por cerca de 40 millones de años.

facts.statement: In 1977, new remains from the Miocene of Peru were described.
facts.quote: En 1977, nuevos restos fueron descritos del Mioceno de Perú.

facts.statement: A third species, S. querejazus, was described in 1991 from the Santa Lucía Formation of early Paleocene southern Bolivia.
facts.quote: Una tercera especie de Sebecus, S. querejazus, fue descrita en 1991 en la formación Santa Lucía, del Paleoceno temprano del sur de Bolivia.

facts.statement: In 1993, Gasparini et al. described Sebecus carajazus, which was later determined to be a writing error for Sebecus querejazus rather than a fourth species.
facts.quote: En 1993, Gasparini et al. describieron Sebecus carajazus. Esta no fue una cuarta especie sino un error de escritura, o lapsus calami, de Sebecus querejazus.

facts.statement: In a 2007 study, Paolillo and Linares reclassified several species, assigning S. huilensis to the genus Langstonia and S. querejazus to the genus Zulmasuchus.
facts.quote: En un estudio sobre los sebécidos publicado en 2007, Paolillo y Linares reclasificaron varias especies. A S. huilensis y S. querejazus les asignaron sus propios géneros, Langstonia y Zulmasuchus, respectivamente

facts.statement: The postcranial skeleton of S. icaeorhinus was virtually unknown until Pol et al. (2012) described postcranial remains of several individuals, including the partially articulated specimen MPEF-PV 1776.
facts.quote: El esqueleto postcraneal de S. icaeorhinus era virtualmente desconocido hasta que Pol et al. (2012) describieron restos postcraneales de varios individuos de esta especie, incluyendo el espécimen parcialmente articulado MPEF-PV 1776, que conservaba la región anterior del dentario (permitiendo la identificación de este individuo con S. icaeorhinus) y la mayor parte del esqueleto postcraneal.

facts.statement: Sebecus elements provided additional evidence of its terrestrial condition, as its legs, especially its femurs, were proportionally longer than those of modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Dichos elementos de Sebecus han provisto de evidencia adicional de su condición terrestre. Sus patas, especialmente sus fémures, eran proprocionalmente más largos que los miembros de los crocodilianos actuales

facts.statement: In 2021, another species was described by Bravo et al. based on remains found in northwestern Argentina.
facts.quote: En 2021 otra especie fue descrita por Bravo et al. con base en restos encontrados en el noroeste de Argentina.

facts.statement: The rock layer containing a partial skull and jaw belongs to the Paleocene Mealla Formation.
facts.quote: La capa de rocas en la que se halló un cráneo parcial y mandíbula son parte de la Formación Mealla del Paleoceno.

facts.statement: This new species was named Sebecus ayrampu after the ayrampu fruit of the Tunilla cactus genus, which resembles the reddish-brown color of the Mealla Formation sediments.
facts.quote: Esta nueva especie fue nombrada como Sebecus ayrampu por el ayrampu (o ayrampo), el fruto de los cactos del género Tunilla, que se asemejan al color pardo rojizo de los sedimentos de la Formación Maella.

facts.statement: Sebecus had an unusually deep and narrow snout compared to other crocodilomorphs.
facts.quote: De manera inusual entre los crocodilomorfos, Sebecus tenía un hocico profundo y estrecho.

facts.statement: The nostrils of Sebecus were located at the very tip of its snout.
facts.quote: Las narinas, o fosas nasales, estaban abiertas anteriormente, en la punta del hocico.

facts.statement: The skull of Sebecus was essentially flat, unlike the raised skulls of many modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: el cráneo de Sebecus está esencialmente nivelado.

facts.statement: Sebecus possessed laterally compressed, serrated teeth known as ziphodont teeth.
facts.quote: Los dientes comprimidos lateralmente y de bordes aserrados, o zifodontos, son característicos de Sebecus y otros sebecosuquios.

facts.statement: The fourth tooth in the lower jaw of Sebecus projected forward to form a canine-like tooth.
facts.quote: El cuarto diente dentario sobresale en la mandíbula inferior para formar una especie de caniniforme.

facts.statement: The first lower jaw tooth of Sebecus was procumbent, fitting between the first and second premaxillary teeth.
facts.quote: El procumbente primer diente dentario se ajustaba entre los dientes premaxilares primero y segundo.

facts.statement: The jaw movement and shearing action of the teeth indicate that Sebecus was a carnivore.
facts.quote: El movimiento de la mandíbula y la acción de tijera de los dientes sugieren que Sebecus era carnívoro.

facts.statement: Sebecus likely consumed food in a manner more similar to theropod dinosaurs than to living crocodilians.
facts.quote: Sebecus probablemente consumía su comida en una manera más similar a la de los dinosaurios terópodos que a los crocodilianos vivientes.

facts.statement: The olfactory bulb of Sebecus was elongated and occupied a significant portion of its brain.
facts.quote: El bulbo olfatorio es alargado y ocupa una parte significativa del cerebro.

facts.statement: The skull and jaw shape of Sebecus provided more space for the adductor muscles that close the jaws.
facts.quote: En Sebecus, la forma del cráneo y mandíbulas provee más espacio para los músculos aductores, que cierran las mandíbulas.

facts.statement: Sebecus likely had a very strong bite but a relatively weak ability to open its jaws.
facts.quote: mientras el cierre de las mandíbulas habría sido muy fuerte, la fuerza de apertura de las mandíbulas habría sido más débil.

facts.statement: Postcranial remains suggest Sebecus had a total body length of 2.2 to 3.1 meters and weighed between 52.2 and 113.5 kilograms.
facts.quote: Les permiten inferir una longitud corporal total de 2.2 a 3.1 metros y un peso de 52.2 a 113.5 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Sebecus has been used to define major groups of crocodilomorphs, including the family Sebecidae and the suborder Sebecosuchia.
facts.quote: Sebecus ha sido usado para definir grandes grupos de crocodiliformes como Sebecidae y Sebecosuchia.

facts.statement: Carvalho et al. (2004) defined the family Sebecidae as the clade including the most recent common ancestor of Sebecus and Libycosuchus and all its descendants.
facts.quote: Carvalho et al. (2004) usaron a Sebecus en su definición de Sebecidae, considerándolo el clado que incluye al más reciente ancestro común de Sebecus y Libycosuchus y a todos sus descendientes.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses have resulted in a polyphyletic Sebecosuchia clade, with some members like Baurusuchus closer to notosuchians and others like Sebecus forming a metasuchian clade more distantly related to Notosuchia.
facts.quote: Varios análisis filogenéticos han resultado en un clado Sebecosuchia polifilético, con algunos miembros como Baurusuchus siendo más cercanos a los notosuquios y otros como Sebecus formando un clado de metasuquios más distantemente relacionados con Notosuchia.

facts.statement: Sebecus lived from the Danian to the Zanclean epochs, approximately 66 to 3.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Danian to Zanclean (66 to 3.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Sebecus was named by Stirton in 1953.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Sebecus (genus), Stirton 1953

facts.statement: The supratemporal fenestrae, two holes in the rear of the skull, were relatively small in Sebecus.
facts.quote: Las fenestras supratemporales, dos agujeros en la zona posterior del cráneo, son relativamente pequeños.

facts.statement: The Eustachian tubes connecting the middle ear to the pharynx were highly complex in crocodilians, including Sebecus.
facts.quote: Las trompas de Eustaquio, que conectan el oído medio con la faringe, son muy complejas en los crocodilianos.

facts.statement: The jaw-opening muscle in Sebecus originated near the top of the skull and inserted on the retroarticular process at the back of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: El músculo depresor que abre las mandíbulas se origina cerca de lo alto del cráneo y se inserta en una proyección de la parte posterior de las mandíbulas, el proceso retroarticular.

facts.statement: Ultrastructural analysis using electron microscopes revealed micro-scratches on Sebecus teeth suggesting a specific method of cutting meat.
facts.quote: Análisis ultraestructurales usando microscopios de electrones han revelado micro-arañazos en los dientes que sugieren esta forma de cortar.

facts.statement: Colbert interpreted the small telencephalon of Sebecus as a sign of primitivism, suggesting an evolutionary trend toward larger brains in crocodilians.
facts.quote: Colbert interpretó el menor telencéfalo de Sebecus como un signo de primitivismo, considerando una tendencia evolutiva hacia un mayor tamaño cerebral en los crocodilianos.

facts.quote: Larsson y Sues (2007) nombraron a este clado Sebecia.
